mainTopic: Finishing the קרבן פסח service: the three groups, the closing of the עזרה, the great crowds, and the details of the bowls and blood
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's description of the קרבן פסח in the עזרה. On שבת, people skinned the animal using each other's shoulders, and the three groups waited in set places until dark. The גמרא brings רבי יצחק's rule that the פסח is slaughtered in three groups of thirty. Because of a ספק in how to read 'קהל, עדה, ישראל', fifty people rotating in and out is enough. אביי and רבא argue whether the עזרה doors closed by a נס or by people, which is a question of relying on a נס. Two ברייתות then describe the huge crowds: the 'פסח מעוכין' in הלל's time, and אגריפס's count of the offerings by their kidneys. The גמרא works out how that count fit the laws of burning the אימורים. Finally, the גמרא explains more details of the משנה: why the gold and silver bowls were kept in separate rows, that שחיטה by a זר is valid, ברב עם הדרת מלך, and אין מעבירין על המצוות. It ends with the sources that the פסח blood is thrown (רבי יוסי הגלילי) on a side of the מזבח with a יסוד (רבי אלעזר).

steps.title: Skinning the פסח when ערב פסח falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains how the קרבן פסח was hung, skinned, and opened on שבת, and how its אימורים were burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, a person puts his hand on his friend's shoulder, and his friend puts his hand on the first person's shoulder. They hang the animal on their arms and skin it. He then cuts it open and takes out its אימורים. He puts them in a large basin, and the כהן burns them on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues mid-sentence from the previous page. It explains how they skinned the פסח on שבת, when they could not use the usual sticks for hanging the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular day, people hung the animal on hooks or on thin poles laid across their shoulders. On שבת those poles may not be handled because of מוקצה. So two people use each other's shoulders as the hanger instead. After skinning, the fats and other parts that go on the מזבח (the אימורים) are removed and burned.

keyTerms.meaning: hangs the animal and skins it
the parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח (fats, kidneys, etc.)
to burn (a קרבן part) on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The first words, 'שחל להיות בשבת', are the end of a sentence that began on the previous page: 'ארבעה עשר שחל להיות בשבת', meaning the fourteenth of ניסן that fell on שבת. Don't read it as a new topic.

phrases.english: (The fourteenth of Nisan) that fell on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Continues from the previous daf: 'ארבעה עשר שחל להיות בשבת'.

phrases.english: he places his hand on his fellow's shoulder,
and his fellow's hand on his own shoulder,
phrases.notes: Their linked arms take the place of the poles, which are מוקצה on שבת.

phrases.english: and he hangs (the animal) and skins it.
He tore it open and removed its sacrificial parts.
He placed them in a large basin,
and (the כהן) burned them on top of the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת, מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ עַל כֶּתֶף חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the פסח service from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, people hang and skin the פסח using each other's shoulders instead of poles. The אימורים are then removed and burned on the מזבח.

steps.title: Where the three groups waited until nightfall on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: On שבת, the groups could not carry their פסח home. Each group waited in a set place until dark and then went out to roast it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first group went out and sat on the הר הבית. The second group waited in the חיל. The third group stayed standing in its place in the עזרה. When it got dark, they went out and roasted their פסח offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what the three groups did after finishing on שבת. Since they could not carry the meat home, each group waited in its assigned spot until שבת ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group moved only as far as it could go without carrying outside the Temple area: הר הבית, the חיל, or the עזרה itself. Roasting is not allowed on שבת, so they had to wait for nightfall. That is also when the eating of the פסח begins.

keyTerms.meaning: a group (here, one of the three groups that brought the פסח)
a low walled area just outside the women's courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה describes three separate groups (כתות) bringing the פסח. This is exactly what the גמרא will now explain.

phrases.english: The first group went out
and sat on the Temple Mount.
The second (group sat) in the rampart area,
and the third stood in its place (in the Temple courtyard).
When it became dark, they went out and roasted their Paschal offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְתָה כַּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וְיָשְׁבָה לָהּ בְּהַר הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the שבת case of the משנה, describing what happens after the service is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, the three groups wait in הר הבית, the חיל, and the עזרה until dark, and only then go out to roast their פסח.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: three groups of thirty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבי יצחק's rule that the פסח is slaughtered only in three groups of at least thirty people each.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יצחק said: The פסח may only be slaughtered in three groups, each made up of thirty people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by stating a rule from רבי יצחק about how many people are needed when the פסח is slaughtered. This explains why the משנה spoke of three groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only described three groups. רבי יצחק turns this into a requirement and adds a minimum size of thirty per group. The next steps will explain where both the 'three' and the 'thirty' come from.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
The Paschal offering is not slaughtered
except in three groups
of thirty people each.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אֵין הַפֶּסַח נִשְׁחָט אֶלָּא בְּשָׁלֹשׁ כִּתּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and sets the size of the three groups mentioned in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסח must be slaughtered in three groups, each of at least thirty people.

steps.title: The source: assembly, congregation, and Israel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יצחק's rule. It answers with the three words in the פסוק: קהל, עדה, and ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The פסוק says 'קהל עדת ישראל': assembly, congregation, and Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יצחק's rule comes from. It answers with the פסוק about the פסח slaughter, 'ושחטו אותו כל קהל עדת ישראל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses three words for the people: קהל, עדה, and ישראל. Each word is understood as a group of at least ten, the way עדה means ten elsewhere (the ten מרגלים). That gives us three groups, but it still doesn't tell us whether they must be together or one after another.

keyTerms.meaning: congregation (a group of at least ten)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
"Assembly," "congregation," and "Israel."
phrases.notes: From שמות יב:ו, 'ושחטו אותו כל קהל עדת ישראל'. Each term counts as a group of ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does the requirement of three groups come from?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three words קהל, עדה, and ישראל in the פסוק each stand for a group of ten.

steps.title: The doubt: all at once or one after another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it is unsure whether the three groups of ten must be present at the same time or one after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are unsure: does it mean all at the same time, or one group after another?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states an open question about how to read the three words. This sets up the next step, which explains how the rule of 'thirty' solves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One reading is that all three tens must be present together, which means thirty people at once. The other reading is that three groups of ten must come one after the other. The גמרא does not decide between them; it treats this as a real ספק.

phrases.english: It is uncertain to us
whether (it means) at the same time
or one after another,

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַפְּקָא לַן אִי בְּבַת אַחַת אִי בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out an unclear point in how to read the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the three groups of ten need to be together (thirty at once) or come one after another?

steps.title: Thirty in each of three groups covers both readings
steps.stepSummary: Since we don't know which reading is right, we require three groups of thirty. That satisfies both possibilities.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore we need three groups of thirty people each. If the rule is 'all at once', we have that, since each group has thirty together. If the rule is 'one after another', we have that too, since there are three groups in a row.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יצחק said 'thirty' in each of three groups. It is a way to be safe and fulfill both readings of the ספק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group of thirty contains three tens standing together, which satisfies the 'at the same time' reading. Having three separate groups in a row satisfies the 'one after another' reading. So the number thirty comes from the ספק, not directly from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: here it is (that requirement is met)

steps.whatToRemember: Three groups of thirty is a safety rule. It is built to satisfy both sides of a ספק about how to read 'קהל, עדה, ישראל'.

phrases.english: Therefore we require

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ כִּתּוֹת שֶׁל שְׁלֹשִׁים שְׁלֹשִׁים בְּנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: three groups of thirty people each.
For if (it must be) at the same time, we have it,
phrases.notes: Each group has thirty (three tens) together.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בָּזֶה אַחַר זֶה — הָא אִיכָּא,
phrases.english: and if (it must be) one after another, we have it.
phrases.notes: There are three groups in a row.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ בָּעֵינַן שָׁלֹשׁ כִּתּוֹת שֶׁל שְׁלֹשִׁים שְׁלֹשִׁים בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the doubt from the previous step by choosing a number that satisfies both readings.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Three groups of thirty fulfill both the 'at once' and the 'one after another' readings of the פסוק.

steps.title: Fifty people are enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a practical result: by rotating people in and out, only fifty people are needed to form three groups of thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore fifty people are also enough. Thirty go in and do the service. Then ten new people go in and ten of the first group leave. Then ten more go in and ten more leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical shortcut that follows from רבי יצחק's rule. You don't need ninety different people; fifty is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first thirty form group one. When ten leave and ten new people enter, the room has a new set of thirty, which counts as group two. Doing it again creates group three. Every group has thirty together, and there are three groups in a row, all with only fifty people in total.
steps.confusionAlert: The groups don't have to be made of completely different people. Swapping out ten at a time is enough to count as a new group of thirty.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule is about having a 'new group' present at each stage, not about the total number of people. That makes the מצוה possible even when few people are there.

phrases.english: Therefore, with fifty it is also enough,
for thirty enter and perform (the service),
ten enter and ten leave,
phrases.notes: This creates the second group of thirty.

phrases.english: ten enter and ten leave.
phrases.notes: This creates the third group of thirty. The total is 30 + 10 + 10 = 50.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ בְּחַמְשִׁין נָמֵי סַגִּיא, דְּעָיְילִי תְּלָתִין וְעָבְדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from the rule of three groups of thirty.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By rotating ten people out and ten new people in twice, fifty people can make up three groups of thirty.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree on how the doors were closed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about the first group entering. It then brings a dispute: אביי says the משנה reads נִנְעֲלוּ ('the doors closed'), and רבא says it reads נוֹעֲלִין ('they close the doors').
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'The first group entered, etc.' It was stated: אביי said, 'We learned "they were closed".' רבא said, 'We learned "they close".'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's line about the first group entering the עזרה, after which the doors were shut. אביי and רבא argue about the exact word the משנה used for shutting the doors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נִנְעֲלוּ means the doors closed on their own once the עזרה was full. נוֹעֲלִין means people actively shut the doors. The dispute is about one word in the משנה, but the next step shows it has a real consequence.

keyTerms.meaning: They were closed / they closed by themselves

phrases.english: "The first group entered, etc."
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: It was stated: Abaye said: We learned "they were closed."
phrases.notes: The doors closed by themselves.

phrases.english: Rava said: We learned "they close."
phrases.notes: People shut the doors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the three groups of thirty and moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the משנה reads נִנְעֲלוּ (closed by themselves). רבא: the משנה reads נוֹעֲלִין (people close them).

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what real difference there is between אביי's version and רבא's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what changes in practice depending on which version is correct. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree the doors ended up shut. The גמרא wants to know whether the argument is only about words or leads to a different law.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the wording dispute in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical legal difference between נִנְעֲלוּ and נוֹעֲלִין.

steps.title: The difference is whether we rely on a miracle
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether we may rely on a נס. According to אביי, everyone who wants to enters and we trust a נס to close the doors in time. According to רבא, people must close the doors, because we do not rely on a נס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is relying on a miracle. אביי said 'they were closed': as many as entered, entered, and we rely on a miracle. רבא said 'they close': we do not rely on a miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the dispute is about relying on a נס. אביי lets people stream in and trusts the doors to shut by themselves; רבא requires people to shut them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, nobody had to stop the crowd; the doors miraculously closed when the עזרה was full, so no one was crushed. For רבא, we may not count on that, so people had to close the doors to prevent dangerous crowding.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying it is generally fine to rely on miracles. He is reading the משנה as describing what actually happened in the עזרה, where a נס regularly closed the doors.

phrases.english: The difference between them is relying on a miracle.
Abaye said: We learned "they were closed";
as many as entered, entered,
phrases.notes: No one stops people from coming in.

phrases.english: and we rely on a miracle.
Rava said: We learned "they close";
and we do not rely on a miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference is whether we rely on a נס to stop overcrowding: אביי yes, רבא no.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a dispute about one word in the משנה into a basic question: may we count on a נס, or must people take action themselves?

steps.title: רבי יהודה's statement about עקביא בן מהללאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי יהודה says עקביא בן מהללאל was never put in נידוי, because no one as wise and sin-fearing as he was ever in the עזרה when it was closed. The word נִנְעֶלֶת seems to fit אביי's version better.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what we learned: רבי יהודה said, 'Heaven forbid that עקביא בן מהללאל was banned, for the עזרה was not closed upon any man in Israel as wise and sin-fearing as עקביא בן מהללאל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another משנה that uses the same word, 'closed', about the עזרה. It is setting up the question of whose version this source supports.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה praises עקביא: even when the עזרה was full and closed, no one there matched him. The form נִנְעֶלֶת ('becomes closed') sounds like אביי's version, where the doors closed by themselves, so it seems to challenge רבא.

phrases.english: And that which we learned: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁעֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל נִתְנַדָּה,
phrases.english: Heaven forbid that Akavya ben Mahalalel was banned,
for the Temple courtyard does not close
phrases.notes: The key word that seems to match אביי.

phrases.english: upon any man in Israel
in wisdom and fear of sin
like Akavya ben Mahalalel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside משנה that uses the 'closing' wording, to test the אביי and רבא dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's version (נוֹעֲלִין), and the question of how each side reads this משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה uses the form נִנְעֶלֶת ('becomes closed'), which sounds like the doors closed by themselves, as אביי says.

steps.title: Both can explain it; אביי's reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says both אביי and רבא can explain רבי יהודה's words according to their own view. אביי reads it: no one in the עזרה when it closed by itself was like עקביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי explains it his way, and רבא explains it his way. אביי explains it his way: There was no one in the עזרה, at the time it closed, from all of Israel as wise and sin-fearing as עקביא בן מהללאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the source does not decide the dispute, since each אמורא can read it his own way. It starts with אביי's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the words fit simply: the עזרה closed by itself, and among everyone inside at that moment, no one matched עקביא. The main point of רבי יהודה's praise stays the same either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains it according to his own view
At the time it closed (by itself)

phrases.english: Abaye explains it according to his view,
and Rava explains it according to his view.
Abaye explains it according to his view:
There was no one in the courtyard at the time it closed
phrases.notes: By itself, through a נס.

phrases.english: from any man in Israel

phrases.aramaic: בְּחׇכְמָה וּבְיִרְאַת חֵטְא כַּעֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל:
phrases.english: as wise and sin-fearing as Akavya ben Mahalalel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, וְרָבָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by showing the source fits both views, starting with אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each side reads the source in line with his own view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wording נִנְעֶלֶת proves the doors closed by themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source can be read either way. For אביי, it means 'when it closed by itself'.

steps.title: רבא's reading of the same statement
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads רבי יהודה's words as: no one in the עזרה when people closed it was like עקביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא explains it his way: There was no one in the עזרה, at the time they closed it upon all Israel, as wise and sin-fearing as עקביא בן מהללאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by showing that רבא can also explain רבי יהודה's words, by reading them as 'when people closed it'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא simply changes the reading to the active form, 'when they close it'. The praise of עקביא is the same, so the source proves nothing either way, and the dispute between אביי and רבא remains open.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי: the doors closed by a נס, and we rely on it. רבא: people closed the doors, and we do not rely on a נס. רבי יהודה's statement about עקביא fits both views.

phrases.english: Rava explains it according to his view:
There was no one in the courtyard at the time they closed it
phrases.notes: People closing the doors.

phrases.english: upon all of Israel

phrases.aramaic: בְּחׇכְמָה וּבְיִרְאַת חֵטְא כַּעֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל.
phrases.english: as wise and sin-fearing as Akavya ben Mahalalel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided answer begun in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording to fit his view.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא reads it as 'when they closed it', so the source fits his view too.

steps.title: Only once was someone crushed in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that no one was ever crushed in the עזרה, except on one פסח in the days of הלל, when an old man was crushed. That year was called 'פסח מעוכין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: No person was ever crushed in the עזרה, except for one פסח in the days of הלל, when one old man was crushed, and they called it 'the פסח of the crushed'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the huge crowds in the עזרה. It says that only once in history was anyone crushed there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the theme of overcrowding raised by the doors. Even with enormous crowds, the עזרה was normally safe, which shows how unusual the one tragedy in הלל's time was. That is why the year was remembered by a special name.

keyTerms.meaning: הלל הזקן, leader of the חכמים in בית שני times

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֵעוֹלָם לָא נִתְמַעֵךְ אָדָם בָּעֲזָרָה,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: No person was ever crushed in the Temple courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִפֶּסַח אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה בִּימֵי הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: except for one Passover that was in the days of Hillel,
on which one old man was crushed,
and they would call it "the Passover of the crushed."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֵעוֹלָם לָא נִתְמַעֵךְ אָדָם בָּעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the doors and overcrowding to a historical ברייתא about crowds in the עזרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No one was ever crushed in the עזרה except once, on the 'פסח מעוכין' in הלל's time.

steps.title: אגריפס המלך counts the Jewish people through the קרבנות פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: אגריפס המלך asked the כהן גדול to count the קרבנות פסח. A kidney was taken from each one, and there were 600,000 pairs, double the number who left מצרים. That count did not include people who were טמא or far away, and every קרבן had more than ten people registered on it. That year was called 'פסח מעובין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Once King אגריפס wanted to see how many Jews there were. He told the כהן גדול, 'Look at the קרבנות פסח.' The כהן גדול took one kidney from each animal. They found 600,000 pairs of kidneys, double the number of people who left מצרים. This did not count people who were טמא or on a far journey. Every קרבן פסח had more than ten people signed up on it. They called that פסח 'the crowded פסח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, continuing the theme of huge crowds at the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every קרבן פסח has a group registered on it, counting the animals gives a rough count of the people. 600,000 pairs of kidneys, with one kidney taken from each animal, means 1,200,000 animals. With over ten people on each, that is more than twelve million people. That is before adding those who were טמא or far away.

keyTerms.meaning: King Agrippa, a king of Israel in Second Temple times
the masses (population) of the Jewish people
a kidney (one of the parts burned on the מזבח)
were registered on it (signed up to eat from this קרבן)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the previous step. There it was 'פסח מעוכין' (with a כ), the פסח when an old man was crushed. Here it is 'פסח מעובין' (with a ב), meaning the crowded פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the setup for the next several steps. The גמרא will question the detail that the כהן גדול 'took a kidney' from each קרבן.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: Once King Agrippa wished
to set his eyes on the multitudes of Israel (to count them).
phrases.notes: It is forbidden to count Jews directly, so an indirect method was used.

phrases.english: He said to the High Priest:
Set your eyes on the Pesach offerings.
phrases.notes: In other words, count the animals.

phrases.english: He took a kidney from each one,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצְאוּ שָׁם שִׁשִּׁים רִיבּוֹא זוּגֵי כְלָיוֹת
phrases.english: and there were found there six hundred thousand pairs of kidneys,
double the number of those who left Egypt.
phrases.notes: 600,000 pairs means 1,200,000 kidneys. Since one kidney was taken from each animal, that is 1,200,000 offerings, double the 600,000 men who left מצרים.

phrases.english: Not counting those who were impure or on a distant journey.
phrases.notes: These people bring פסח שני instead.

phrases.english: And there was not a single Pesach offering

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא נִמְנוּ עָלָיו יוֹתֵר מֵעֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: that did not have more than ten people registered on it.
And they called it 'the crowded Pesach.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פַּעַם אַחַת בִּיקֵּשׁ אַגְרִיפַּס הַמֶּלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the huge Pesach crowds from the previous ברייתא about פסח מעוכין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קרבנות פסח were counted with kidneys: 1,200,000 offerings (600,000 pairs of kidneys), double those who left מצרים, each with more than ten people, showing an enormous crowd.

steps.title: How could he take a kidney that must be burned on the altar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the כהן גדול could take the kidney. The kidney is one of the parts that must be burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took a kidney? But it needs to be burned on the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions a detail in the story. The kidneys belong on the מזבח, so how could they be taken away for counting?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kidneys are among the אימורים, the parts of a קרבן that must be burned on the מזבח. Removing them for a count seems to take away something that belongs to the מזבח.

phrases.english: He took a kidney?
But it needs to be burned (on the altar)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a detail of the ברייתא in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The detail that the כהן גדול took a kidney from each קרבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Kidneys must be burned on the מזבח, so they cannot simply be taken away.

steps.title: He burned the kidneys afterward
steps.stepSummary: First answer: he took the kidneys to count them and burned them afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: He later went back and burned them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the kidneys were not lost. They were counted first and burned later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the kidney was only a delay, so the kidney still reached the מזבח in the end. The next step will ask whether such a delayed burning is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: that he later went back and burned them

phrases.english: He later went back and burned them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: the kidneys were only delayed, not withheld.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Taking the kidney means it never got burned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The kidneys were counted first and burned later.

steps.title: The fats of different offerings may not be mixed together
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'והקטירו' (burn IT), in the singular. This teaches that fats from one קרבן may not be mixed with another's. Burning all the collected kidneys together would mix them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'והקטירו' (he shall burn IT). This teaches that he may not mix the fats of one קרבן with another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer. If all the kidneys were gathered and burned later, they would be burned mixed together, which the פסוק forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The singular word 'it' teaches that each קרבן's fats must be burned as their own unit. A pile of kidneys from many different קרבנות burned together would break this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: its fats (the parts burned on the מזבח)

phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'And he shall burn it,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ג:יא

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְעָרֵב חֲלָבָיו שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה!
phrases.english: meaning he may not mix the fats of this one with that one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that he burned the kidneys later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Burning them later means burning them together, and the singular 'והקטירו' forbids mixing fats of different קרבנות.

steps.title: He burned the kidneys one by one
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: he burned each kidney separately, so nothing was mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He later burned them one at a time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adjusts the answer. The kidneys were burned later, but each one separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning each kidney by itself avoids mixing different קרבנות. This answers the problem raised by 'והקטירו'.

phrases.english: He later went back and burned them one by one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by refining the answer of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The kidneys were burned together in one mixed batch.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each kidney was burned on its own, so nothing was mixed.

steps.title: All parts of one offering must be burned together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'והקטירם' (burn THEM) as requiring all the parts of one קרבן to be burned together. A kidney burned later, apart from the rest of its animal's fats, breaks this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא taught: 'והקטירם' (he shall burn THEM) teaches that all of it must be burned together, as one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second answer. The kidney cannot be burned separately from the other fats of its own animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two rules here. 'והקטירו' means do not mix different animals. 'והקטירם' means keep all of one animal's parts together. Holding back a kidney and burning it alone afterward splits it from the other parts of its own קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: all of it together at once

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: 'And he shall burn them,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ג:טז

phrases.english: meaning that all of it must be (burned) together!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that each kidney was burned separately afterward.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All the אימורים of one קרבן must be burned together, so a kidney may not be burned apart from the rest of its animal.

steps.title: He only held the kidney briefly until a token replaced it
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: the kidney was only held for a moment. The כהן גדול took it until they gave him some other object to count, and then the kidney went back to be burned properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was just a brief grab. He took the kidney from them until they gave him something else (to count with).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops both earlier answers and explains that the kidneys were never kept. Each kidney was swapped right away for a counting token.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the kidney was returned at once, it was burned together with its own animal's fats, as 'והקטירם' requires. It was also never mixed with other animals, as 'והקטירו' requires. What was actually counted afterward were the replacement tokens.
steps.whatToRemember: The kidney count was really a token count. Each kidney was held only briefly and exchanged for another object. This way, the burning laws of 'והקטירו' (do not mix different animals) and 'והקטירם' (burn one animal's parts together) were both kept.

phrases.english: Rather: it was merely a brief grab,
that he took (the kidneys) from them
until they gave him something else (in its place).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 with a new explanation that replaces the answers of steps 17 and 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the action: a temporary hold with a substitute token.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The kidneys were kept for counting and burned later, either together or one by one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each kidney was held only for a moment and returned. The substitute objects were what got counted.

steps.title: Why were gold and silver bowls kept in separate rows?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which said the כהנים stood in rows with all-gold or all-silver bowls, never mixed. It asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The כהנים stood in rows, etc.' What is the reason (that gold and silver bowls were not mixed in one row)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and asks for its reason. This sets up the next steps, where it will suggest an answer, reject it, and give a final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says each row had only one type of bowl. The גמרא wants to know why this arrangement was needed.

phrases.english: 'The priests stand in rows, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: rows of all-silver or all-gold bowls, never mixed.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֲנִים עוֹמְדִין שׁוּרוֹת וְכוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגריפס discussion and returns to analyzing the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה kept gold and silver bowls in separate rows.

steps.title: Suggested reason: to stop someone swapping gold for silver
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a reason. Maybe a כהן would take a gold bowl for himself and slip a silver one into its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the reason is that maybe someone would take a gold bowl and bring in a silver one in its place,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason: to prevent theft by swapping bowls. It will test this suggestion right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a row had both metals, a gold bowl could quietly be replaced with a silver one. Keeping each row all one metal would make such a swap easy to notice.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say: perhaps
they would take a gold one and bring in a silver one —

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דִּילְמָא שָׁקְלִי דְּדַהֲבָא וּמְעַיְּילִי דְּכַסְפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggested reason: to prevent swapping gold bowls for silver ones. This is about to be rejected.

steps.title: The same worry exists even within an all-gold row
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected. Even in an all-gold row, someone could take a bowl worth 200 and put back one worth 100, so separating the metals does not prevent theft.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, maybe someone would take a bowl worth two hundred and bring in one worth one hundred!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the theft reason. Separating gold from silver does not actually stop a swap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gold bowls themselves come in different values. If theft were the concern, the משנה's arrangement would not solve it, so theft cannot be the reason.

phrases.english: Here too, perhaps

phrases.aramaic: שָׁקְלִי בַּר מָאתַן וּמְעַיְּילִי בַּר מְאָה!
phrases.english: they would take one worth two hundred and bring in one worth one hundred!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי, דִּילְמָא שָׁקְלִי בַּר מָאתַן וּמְעַיְּילִי בַּר מְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested reason of step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects theft-prevention as the reason for separate rows.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The arrangement would not prevent theft, because bowls of the same metal also differ in value.

steps.title: The real reason: it looks nicer
steps.stepSummary: Conclusion: the rows were kept all-gold or all-silver simply because it looks more beautiful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, (the reason is) that this way is more beautiful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. The separate rows were for beauty, not to prevent theft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since theft was ruled out, the reason is honoring the עבודה with a neat, attractive arrangement. Matching rows look more dignified.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהנים stood in rows of all-gold or all-silver bowls for beauty, not as a guard against theft.

phrases.english: Rather, because this way is more beautiful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason of step 23 with the final answer to the question of step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Gold and silver bowls were kept in separate rows for beauty.

steps.title: No bowls in the Temple had flat bottoms, except the frankincense bowls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the bowls had no flat bottoms. It then brings a ברייתא: all bowls in the מקדש lacked flat bottoms, except the לבונה bowls of the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the bowls had no flat bottoms. A ברייתא teaches: none of the bowls in the מקדש had flat bottoms, except the bowls of frankincense of the לחם הפנים. Those needed flat bottoms because they were placed on the bread, and a pointed bottom could break it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the next phrase in the משנה and adds a ברייתא that widens the rule to all bowls in the מקדש, with one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bowls had no flat bottoms so that the כהנים could not set them down and let the blood thicken. The bowls of לבונה were different. They were placed on the delicate לחם הפנים, so a pointed bottom could poke into the bread and break it.

keyTerms.meaning: Bowls, here the bowls used in the מקדש
The showbread placed on the שולחן
And it would break or crumble

phrases.english: "And the bowls did not have flat bottoms, etc."
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
All the bowls that were in the Temple
did not have flat bottoms,
except for the bowls of frankincense
of the showbread,
since perhaps they would rest them on it and the bread would break.
phrases.notes: So those bowls needed flat bottoms

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the משנה after the discussion of gold and silver rows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every bowl in the מקדש lacked a flat bottom, except the לבונה bowls of the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: Must the slaughterer be a regular ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said 'an ישראל slaughtered.' The גמרא asks whether this means a non-ישראל, such as a כהן or לוי, may not slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'An ישראל slaughtered and the כהן received.' Is it not good enough if someone who is not an ישראל slaughters?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה's wording. Why does it specifically say that an ישראל slaughtered?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, the משנה seems to require that the slaughterer be a regular ישראל. That cannot be right, since a כהן may certainly slaughter. So the גמרא asks what this wording is meant to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Received, meaning caught the blood in a bowl

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not really suggesting that a כהן may not slaughter. It is asking why the משנה chose this wording.

phrases.english: "An Israelite slaughtered and the priest received, etc."
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: Is it not sufficient if it is not an Israelite?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה specify that an ישראל slaughtered?

steps.title: The point is that slaughter by a non-priest is valid
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions an ישראל to teach that שחיטה done by a זר is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: That itself is what the משנה is teaching us: slaughter done by a non-כהן is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not limiting the slaughter to an ישראל. It is showing that even an ישראל may slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ישראל' is not a requirement. It shows the lowest level of person who may still slaughter: a זר, someone who is not a כהן. Since a non-כהן may slaughter, a כהן certainly may.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of קרבנות: שחיטה does not require a כהן.

phrases.english: This itself it teaches us:
that slaughter by a non-priest is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word 'ישראל'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording teaches that שחיטה by a זר is valid.

steps.title: From receiving the blood onward, only priests may do the work
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's words 'and the כהן received' teach that from קבלה onward, the service must be done by a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the כהן received': this teaches us that from receiving the blood and onward, the work is a מצוה for the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of the same משנה phrase, which contrasts the כהן with the ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה deliberately places two people side by side. The ישראל slaughters, and the כהן receives. This shows exactly where the requirement of כהונה begins: at קבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: From receiving the blood and onward
A מצוה that only כהנים may do

steps.whatToRemember: שחיטה may be done by anyone. Starting from קבלה, only a כהן may do the work.

phrases.english: "And the priest received."
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: This teaches us
that from receiving onward it is a commandment of the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the משנה's phrase.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The work is limited to כהנים starting from קבלה.

steps.title: Passing the bowl shows that carrying without walking counts
steps.stepSummary: Since the כהנים passed the bowls from hand to hand, the גמרא suggests a proof that הולכה without walking is valid הולכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'he passes it to his fellow.' Learn from this that carrying the blood without walking counts as carrying!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove an open question from the משנה's description of passing the bowl down the row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הולכה, bringing the blood to the מזבח, is one of the four main עבודות. The question is whether a כהן must walk with the blood. In the row, each כהן just stood and handed the bowl on, which seems to show that walking is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: He gives it to his fellow
Bringing the blood to the מזבח

phrases.english: "He gives it to his fellow."
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: Learn from this:
carrying without walking is considered carrying!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New phrase of the משנה, used as a proof for an open question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether הולכה without walking is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's description of כהנים passing the bowl from hand to hand

steps.title: Maybe each priest moved a little
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Perhaps each כהן took a small step while passing the bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he moves a little.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof. The משנה does not clearly say the כהנים stood completely still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each כהן moved his feet slightly, then real walking took place. So the משנה cannot prove that הולכה without walking is valid, and the question stays open.

phrases.english: Perhaps he moves a little.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only; the question itself is not settled.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה allows for the possibility that the כהנים did walk a little.

steps.title: So why did they use rows at all?
steps.stepSummary: If walking was still needed, the גמרא asks what the system of passing bowls down the rows comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what does this teach us?
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the proof, the גמרא asks what purpose the long rows of כהנים served. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One כהן could simply have walked the blood to the מזבח himself. So there must be some other reason for using a whole chain of כהנים.

phrases.english: But rather, what does it teach us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the rejection: if not a proof about הולכה, then what?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the purpose of the rows of כהנים?

steps.title: Many people honor the King
steps.stepSummary: The rows were meant to involve many כהנים, following ברב עם הדרת מלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us: 'In the multitude of people is the King's glory.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the chain of כהנים existed to bring honor to ה׳ by including many people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rows were not a legal requirement for הולכה. The point was to involve as many כהנים as possible, because a מצוה done by a crowd brings more honor to the King.

keyTerms.meaning: In a multitude of people is the King's glory (משלי יד:כח)

steps.whatToRemember: The rows of כהנים were for ברב עם הדרת מלך. They do not prove anything about הולכה.

phrases.english: It teaches us this:
"In the multitude of people is the King's glory."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rows were for ברב עם הדרת מלך.

steps.title: Taking the full bowl first supports ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says each כהן took the full bowl and then returned the empty one, not the other way around. This supports רבי שמעון בן לקיש's rule: אין מעבירין על המצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He receives the full one and returns the empty one.' But not the opposite. This supports רבי שמעון בן לקיש, who said: we do not pass over מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices the order in the משנה's wording and uses it to support an אמורא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full bowl carries the מצוה, so the כהן takes it first. Only afterward does he hand back the empty bowl. Doing it in reverse would mean delaying a מצוה that is right in front of him, which is what רבי שמעון בן לקיש forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not pass over or delay מצוות

steps.whatToRemember: When a מצוה comes to your hand, do it first. Do not set it aside for something else (אין מעבירין על המצוות).
steps.whyThisMatters: אין מעבירין על המצוות is a well-known rule that is used all across ש״ס and in practical הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: קִבֵּל אֶת הַמָּלֵא וּמַחְזִיר אֶת הָרֵיקָן וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: "He received the full one and returns the empty one, etc."
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: But the opposite, no.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
as Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
One does not pass over מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New phrase of the משנה, used as support for an אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון בן לקיש's rule: אין מעבירין על המצוות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order in the משנה: take the full bowl first, then return the empty one

steps.title: Which תנא holds that the פסח blood is thrown?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the כהן near the מזבח and asks which תנא requires זריקה for the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The כהן closest to the מזבח' throws the blood. Who is the תנא who holds that the פסח needs throwing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, which says the כהן near the מזבח throws the blood. It asks whose opinion this is, and in doing so sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah never explicitly says how the blood of a פסח is placed on the מזבח. So the משנה's assumption that it is thrown (זריקה), and not just poured out, must follow a particular תנא. The גמרא wants to know who that is.

keyTerms.meaning: Throwing the blood from the bowl onto the wall of the מזבח
Who is the תנא? (Whose opinion is this?)
Etc. (the quote from the משנה continues)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'מאן תנא' as an attack. The גמרא is not challenging the משנה. It is only asking for the source of its assumption.

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] 'The priest closest to the altar,' etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה: the כהן closest to the מזבח throws the blood

phrases.english: Who is the Tanna who holds the Paschal lamb is done with throwing?
phrases.notes: Throwing, as opposed to pouring (שפיכה)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of passing the bowls (steps 30-34) and turns to the next clause of the משנה, the act of throwing itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that the blood of the פסח requires זריקה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: It is רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא identifies the opinion as that of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question: the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a short answer that names the תנא. The proof that רבי יוסי הגלילי actually holds this comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: The ברייתא: plural 'their blood' includes בכור, מעשר and פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the plural words 'דָּמָם' and 'חֶלְבָּם' that בכור, מעשר and פסח all need blood and fats placed on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי הגלילי says, the פסוק says 'Their blood you shall throw on the מזבח, and their fat you shall burn.' It does not say 'its blood' but 'their blood.' It does not say 'its fat' but 'their fat.' This teaches about בכור, מעשר and פסח, that they all need their blood and fats put on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove רב חסדא's answer. The פסוק about בכור says 'their blood' (דָּמָם) in the plural, so רבי יוסי הגלילי includes the פסח. Since that פסוק says 'תִּזְרוֹק', the פסח is also done with זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is talking about a בכור, so it should have said 'its blood' in the singular. The plural 'their blood' tells us that other similar קרבנות, namely מעשר and פסח, are included. Since the פסוק says 'תִּזְרוֹק' (throw), the פסח gets זריקה too, which matches our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal brought as a קרבן
The fats and parts of the animal burned on the מזבח
Placing the blood on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why our משנה describes the פסח with זריקה. That is the method written in the בכור פסוק, which רבי יוסי הגלילי applies to the פסח as well.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
'Their blood you shall throw upon the altar
phrases.notes: במדבר יח:יז, said about בכור

phrases.english: and their fat you shall burn' —
It does not say 'its blood' but 'their blood.'
It does not say 'its fat' but 'their fat.'
This teaches about the firstborn, the tithe animal, and the Paschal lamb,
that they require placing of blood and sacrificial parts
on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's answer with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the פסח requires זריקה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the plural 'דָּמָם תִּזְרוֹק' (במדבר יח:יז) as including מעשר and פסח with בכור.

steps.title: How do we know the blood needs the יסוד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the blood of these קרבנות must be thrown on a side of the מזבח that has a יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that they need the יסוד?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה said the כהן throws the blood 'opposite the יסוד.' The גמרא asks where that requirement comes from, and so sets up רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא taught only that the blood goes on the מזבח. It did not say which part. The משנה adds that it goes where there is a יסוד (the base), so the גמרא looks for a source for that detail.

keyTerms.meaning: The base of the מזבח, which did not go all the way around it

steps.confusionAlert: The יסוד was not on every side of the מזבח. So 'needs the יסוד' means the blood must be thrown on a side that has the base underneath.

phrases.english: From where do we know that they require a base?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא and asks for an additional detail: where on the מזבח the blood goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the blood of the פסח (and בכור and מעשר) must be thrown where there is a יסוד.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: A גזירה שוה from עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns from the shared word 'זריקה' that, just like an עולה, the פסח needs a יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: We learn it from 'זריקה' and 'זריקה' from an עולה. Here it says 'Their blood you shall throw on the מזבח,' and there it says 'The sons of Aharon, the כהנים, shall throw its blood on the מזבח all around.' Just as an עולה needs a יסוד, so too a פסח needs a יסוד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers with a גזירה שוה. The same word 'throw' appears for the פסח and for the עולה, so the עולה's rule of needing a יסוד carries over to the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עולה is already known to need a יסוד. The word 'זריקה' links the two פסוקים, so the rules of the עולה pass over to the פסח. This gives a source for the משנה's phrase 'opposite the יסוד.'

keyTerms.meaning: It comes [is learned] through a גזירה שוה
It is written here / it is written there (the classic גזירה שוה formula)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסח is thrown (זריקה) according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, from the plural 'דָּמָם'. It must be thrown where there is a יסוד, learned by רבי אלעזר through a גזירה שוה of 'זריקה זריקה' from עולה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
It is derived from 'sprinkling' 'sprinkling' from the burnt-offering.
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה based on the same word

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״אֶת דָּמָם תִּזְרוֹק עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״,
phrases.english: It is written here: 'Their blood you shall throw upon the altar,'
and it is written there:
'And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall throw
phrases.notes: ויקרא א:יא, said about עולה

phrases.english: its blood upon the altar round about,'
just as a burnt-offering requires a base —
so too the Paschal lamb also requires a base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'זריקה' from עולה teaches that the פסח requires a יסוד.
